title: Ratification of the Thirteenth Amendment
summary: Congress passed the Thirteenth Amendment in January 1865, and it was ratified on 6 December 1865. It abolished slavery and involuntary servitude throughout the United States, except as punishment for a crime of which a person has been duly convicted, and gave Congress power to enforce it.

uncertainty.note: Start is House passage; the Senate had passed it in April 1864. End is completion of ratification.

where.modern_name: United States Capitol, Washington, D.C., USA
where.historical_name: Washington, D.C., United States (Congress); ratified by state legislatures

importance.justification: Constitutional abolition of chattel slavery in the United States.

sources.title: 13th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution: Abolition of Slavery (1865)
sources.publisher: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration

reviewer_note: Pin is the Capitol where Congress passed it; ratification was by state legislatures nationwide. NARA gives January 31, 1865 as the date of congressional passage and 1 February 1865 for presidential approval of the resolution.
